summary: Giulia Porru worked in linguistics and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. under Giacomo Devoto at the University of Florence around 1933–1937, where she later served as Professore incaricato di filologia Germanica in 1946.
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 2010, she held posts at both Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Giuliana Stramiglioni was a scholar of Japanology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (1938), the University of Tokyo teaching Italian (~1938–1965), and Sapienza University of Rome as Professor of Japanese (1965–1985).

Giuseppe Bardelli worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at the University of Pisa (1843, 1849–1851, 1862), the Laurentian Library (1852), and the Istituto di Studi Superiori di Firenze (1859–1862).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who held posts at the University of Bologna as professor of Hebrew and Oriental languages (1797, ~1803–1831), Bologna University Library (1803), and as Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library from 1833.

Giuseppe De Lorenzo studied at the University of Naples Federico II (~1889–1893) and under Karl Eugen Neumann. Working in Buddhist studies, he was a PD (1897) and Professor of Geology and Physical Geography (1905–1941) at the University of Naples Federico II.
Giuseppe Maria da Gargnano was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome and served as vice-prefect at the Tibet Mission in 1758.
Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797) and later held a post there from circa 1803 to 1831.

Giuseppe Toscano was a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (1938–1942) and served as Director of the Museo d'Arte Cinese ed Etnografico from circa 1965 to 1988.

Giuseppe Tucci studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca. A scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology, he taught in India (1925–1930), at Naples (~1929–1932), and at Sapienza University of Rome (1932–1969).

Giuseppe Turrini was an Indologist who studied at the University of Padua and University of Pisa, learning from Giuseppe Bardelli and Gaspare Gorresio. In 1860, he became Professore ordinario di filologia indo-europea at the University of Bologna.

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under Su Bai, Shichang Ma, Chongfeng Li, and Angela Falco Howard, and was affiliated with Peking University as of 2017.

Giuseppina Scalabrino Borsani was an Indology scholar who studied under Ambrogio Ballini at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (~1929–1933). She later served as an assistant at the same university from 1954 to 1980.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (1926) and served as a professor at Toyo University from 1927.

Glenn H. Mullin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, and Ngawang Dhargyey. In 1984, he founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and the traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Glyn Richards worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Wales, Oxford, and McMaster. He held posts at McMaster (1968–1970), Carleton University (1970–1973), and the University of Stirling (1973–1990), where he headed Religious Studies.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Uma Shankar Vyas at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Godabarish Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and served as Director at the University of Madras.

Godamune Chullanaga is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the Indian Cultural Centre, Sri Jinarathana Vocational Training Center, University of Kelaniya (MA, 2003), and the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka (Diploma, 2020).
